newsitem.title: UK: Cardoso sees Brazil pension reform by mid-97 - paper
newsitem.headline: Cardoso sees Brazil pension reform by mid-97 - paper

text.p: Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said proposed reforms to the country's social security system could be achieved by the middle of the year, a British newspaper said on Tuesday,

In an interview with the Financial Times, Cardoso said the likely success of a constitutional amendment to allow for the re-election of a sitting president would provide momentum to push through crucial economic reforms in 1997.
The social security reforms centre on pensions to public servants, who become eligible for pay-outs after only 10 to 12 years of contributions, the Financial Times said.

Fiscal reforms to reallocate revenue, spending and tax collection between Brazil's states and its federal government would be more difficult but could be done by the end of the year, Cardose told the newspaper.

Reforms in Brazil are needed to curb government spending in order to keep inflation under control. On Monday, Cardoso said at a conference in London Brazil's 1997 inflation was likely to fall to around seven percent from an annual 10 percent in 1996.
